title: release-eng: add `rw-backport` CLI to automate cherry-picks + provenance for LTS backports
author: Connor O'Brien
description:
Context: For Runtime LTS patches we’re doing a lot of manual work: cherry-pick commits, resolve conflicts, open PRs against runtime-*-lts branches, and then later reconstruct provenance (which PR/issue drove the backport, what commit(s) were picked, what tests/CI ran). This PR introduces a small, repo-local CLI called `rw-backport` that standardizes the backport workflow and produces an audit-friendly trail.

What this adds: (1) `rw-backport` CLI (Python) that can take a source PR number or a list of commit SHAs and generate a backport branch + PR against a target branch (e.g. `runtime-1.20-lts`), (2) standardized commit message trailers for provenance: `Backport-of: redwood#<pr>`, `Cherry-picked-from: <sha>`, `Requested-by: <linear/jira/customer>`, plus optional `Risk: low|medium|high`, (3) a backport PR template populated with provenance + checklist links to LTS gates, (4) optional GitHub label automation (`needs-backport`, `backport-created`, `backport-risk-high`) to keep the queue tracker accurate.

Usage examples: `./tools/rw-backport --pr 8429 --target runtime-1.20-lts --labels backport-risk-low --requested-by ENG-4825` and `./tools/rw-backport --commits a1b2c3d e4f5a6b --target runtime-1.20-lts --dry-run`.

Design notes: We intentionally keep this tool “thin” (git + GitHub API + text templating). It does not attempt to auto-resolve conflicts. It stops at the first conflict and prints a minimal-diff strategy checklist + suggested commands. It also does not merge PRs; go/no-go stays with Release Eng + Runtime + SRE gates.

Security: tool uses a GitHub token from env (`GITHUB_TOKEN` or `RW_GH_TOKEN`) and only requests repo-scoped actions required to create branches/PRs/labels. No secrets are logged; debug output redacts tokens.

Testing: added unit tests for message trailers + PR body rendering; integration test is a dry-run mode that validates local git state and prints the planned actions without mutating remote.

Rollout: We’ll dogfood for runtime-1.20-lts.0 RCs. If this stabilizes, we can move it to a shared release-eng tools repo later; for now keeping it in-monorepo reduces friction.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): (a) hook into CI to post backport provenance as a build artifact, (b) make `--requested-by` auto-resolve Linear issues to titles, (c) add a `--batch` mode for backport queues.

Refs: ENG-4825, ENG-4823; motivated in part by SUP-3950 where we needed a clean link from customer regression -> PR -> backported commit -> released artifact.

conversation:
Noah Patel (Runtime LTS architect): This is great—biggest concern is minimizing accidental semantic drift in backports. Can we make the tool default to “single-commit cherry-picks only” unless explicitly asked to pick a merge commit? Connor O'Brien (author): Yep. Today it enumerates the PR’s commits and cherry-picks each one. It refuses merge commits by default (detects multiple parents) unless `--allow-merge-commits` is provided. I’ll add that to the help + docs.

Sahana Iyer (CI/build automation): Can we ensure we don’t accidentally run this from a dirty working tree? Also, please make sure the branch name is deterministic enough for automation (queue tracking). Connor O'Brien: Added guard: abort if `git status --porcelain` non-empty unless `--force`. Branch naming: `backport/<target>/<source_pr>-<shortsha>`; can override via `--branch`. Also writing a `.rw-backport.json` file into the branch with metadata (non-secret) so we can parse later.

Marcus Lin (Artifact signing/provenance security reviewer): Token handling looks fine but please avoid printing request headers on debug. Also we should redact `Authorization` if any exception dumps request objects. Connor O'Brien: Good catch. Swapped to a small wrapper that never logs headers; errors print status + endpoint + request id only. Added unit test for redaction.

Sean Gallagher (SRE reliability gate owner): In the PR body template can we include a checklist item that references the perf canary run and rollback criteria? Otherwise people will forget during RC crunch. Connor O'Brien: Added to the backport PR template: “Perf-canary run link” + “Meets LTS regression gates” + “Rollback plan validated” with pointers to the runbook.

Omar El-Sayed (Runtime backport owner): Conflict UX: can we print the exact commit that failed and suggest `git cherry-pick --abort`? Also prefer we keep the resulting commit messages stable. Connor O'Brien: Updated output to print failing commit SHA + subject, plus explicit abort/continue guidance. Commit messages now always include trailers in a stable order; also added `--no-edit` behavior unless user passes `--edit`.

Requested changes (round 1): (1) add `--allow-merge-commits` gate + docs, (2) ensure dirty tree guard, (3) template includes perf gates, (4) token logging redaction. Author pushed updates.

Approvals: Sahana Iyer approved. Noah Patel approved after verifying branch naming + merge commit refusal. Marcus Lin approved after redaction fix. Sean Gallagher approved template update.

Merge: Connor O'Brien merged via squash after green CI. Post-merge note: We’ll trial on the next runtime-1.20-lts RC and iterate based on conflict rates + queue tracker feedback.
release_notes: Internal: added `rw-backport` CLI to standardize LTS backport cherry-picks and open backport PRs with provenance trailers.
Internal: added backport PR template with SRE perf gate checklist and audit-friendly metadata.
